subject: Chat throughput throttle - customer-facing advisory & temporary configs
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@quickpay.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@quickpay.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:14:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production chat sessions - intermittent 3-8s token latency spikes

Hi Rohan / team,

We started seeing noticeable latency in our live-chat experience this morning around 09:05 PDT. Users report that streaming responses stall for multiple seconds between token bursts (3-8s gaps); overall throughput is fine but interactive feel is degraded and some messages time out in our client after 12s. This is impacting two of our high-traffic queues (payments disputes).

What we observed in-app: short stalls that sometimes recover mid-response; no obvious correlation with traffic spikes on our side. We've pinned a few trace IDs in our client logs and included one below. Can you confirm whether there are known degradations in the us-west region and any immediate workarounds we can apply?

Trace IDs: 7d9f-qp-1120, 7d9f-qp-1127

Thanks — we have a midday support push and need a quick mitigation if possible.

—Emily
Emily Carter
Sr. Engineering Manager, Chat
QuickPay
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@quickpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:28:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production chat sessions - intermittent 3-8s token latency spikes

Hi Emily — thanks for the quick flag and the trace IDs. We're seeing correlated alerts for increased per-token latency in the us-west serving tier starting ~09:02 PDT. Short summary of immediate triage steps we are taking now: 

- Routing: forcing traffic from your production pool to a nearby dedicated capacity pool (us-west-2-dedicated) to avoid shared-edge queuing. This change is live and should be transparent.
- Fallback: enabling a non-streaming fallback for requests that exceed 10s to avoid stalling the client (we'll return a completed response instead of streaming).
- Model variant: switching your default route to the quantized v1-small-vq variant which reduces kernel contention for long-token sequences; quality impact should be minimal for the payments flows.
- Client suggestion: reduce client max_tokens_per_chunk to 128 and set a 6s client-side token gap retry to avoid perceiving stalls as timeouts. 

I attached a short config snippet with the temporary changes (temp_config_snippet.txt) and an incident timeline we'll update. We'll monitor the effect over the next 30 minutes and follow up with measurable latency numbers. 

Short-term ask from you: can your team enable the non-streaming fallback in your SDK (one-line toggle) for the next 6 hours so we can prevent timeouts while we finish the RCA? I can send the exact SDK flag if useful.

Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@quickpay.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:05:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production chat sessions - intermittent 3-8s token latency spikes

Emily — quick note from the account side: we've applied the routing override and confirmed your traffic is on the dedicated pool. Early telemetry (09:30 PDT) shows reduced token-gap frequency for the test traces you shared.

Action items I'm taking now:
- Opening a ticket with infra to investigate autoscaler behavior that may have delayed new nodes behind a kernel-selection regression (assigning to Infra team).
- Logging a formal support case HS-58291 for tracking credits and SLA exception requests; I'll update you on credits by EOB today.

If you want us to flip your SDK toggle to non-streaming on our hosted config for you, we can do that immediately and then revert once the fix is live. Let me know which option you prefer.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:40:21 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production chat sessions - intermittent 3-8s token latency spikes

FYI — rolling summary for the internal postmortem thread. Key findings so far (preliminary):
- Root trigger: a recent runtime kernel selection patch (deployed at 08:48 PDT) led to suboptimal kernel paths for quantized long-context workloads, increasing per-token scheduling latency under mixed workloads.
- Autoscaler interaction: slow scale-up of certain shared pools (due to conservative provisioning thresholds) amplified the impact during a small traffic burst at 09:01–09:06 PDT.
- Customer impact: intermittent 3–8s token gaps for ~12% of streaming requests on QuickPay's queues between 09:05–09:35 PDT.

Immediate mitigations applied: routing override to dedicated pool, non-streaming fallback enabled, model variant switch to quantized v1-small-vq, client chunking recommendation.

Next steps for RCA:
- Infra to revert the kernel selection patch to canary and run perf tests on quantized long-context models.
- Runtime team to add a fast-fail path for token-scheduling stalls (short-term gate).
- Product to coordinate a communication plan and customer crediting.

I'll own the postmortem doc and share a draft by end of day Monday. Attaching an interim timeline (incident_timeline.pdf).

—Rohan
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@quickpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — 2026-09-18 us-west streaming latency event

Hi Emily — thanks again for your patience while we completed the initial RCA and mitigations. Short post-incident recap and customer-facing actions: 

What happened (plain language): a runtime optimization deployed on 09/18 increased per-token scheduling time for some quantized, long-context streaming workloads. That interacted with our autoscaler behavior and caused intermittent stalls (3–8s gaps) for a subset of streaming responses.

What we did for QuickPay:
- Immediately routed production traffic to a dedicated pool to remove shared-edge contention.
- Enabled a non-streaming fallback to avoid client timeouts while we validated fixes.
- Switched your default route to the quantized v1-small-vq variant and pushed a recommended client chunking change (max_tokens_per_chunk=128).
- Issued a one-time service credit for the affected window (details attached: service_credit_ack.txt).

What we're changing (platform actions):
- Reverting the kernel selection change from 09/18 for all shared pools and re-deploying after perf validation.
- Autoscaler tuning: lowering the conservative scaling threshold and adding a faster warm-up path for pools handling long-context streaming workloads.
- Runtime guard: adding a fast-fail token-schedule detection and automatic short-circuit to the non-streaming response path.

Timeline and evidence: see attached incident_timeline.pdf and our RCA draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-09-18-chat-latency.

Recommended customer actions (short term):
- Keep the non-streaming fallback enabled for another 12–24 hours if you expect peak traffic; we will notify you before reverting.
- If you prefer, we can roll the fallback flag from the hosted config for you — reply with consent and we'll flip it.

Follow-up: I'll share the finalized postmortem doc on our Drive link by EOD Monday and schedule a 30-minute sync if you'd like to walk through the RCA.

Apologies for the disruption — we know how critical low-latency streaming is for your payments flows and are prioritizing the runtime and autoscaler fixes accordingly.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
